district.name: Gadag
district.description: Land of classical Kannada literature and stepwells, Gadag features Lakkundi's 50+ Chalukyan temples and 101 stepwells, Veeranarayana Temple where poet Kumara Vyasa wrote the Mahabharata, and Trikuteshwara Temple.
district.descriptionKannada: ಕನ್ನಡ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಿಗಳ ನಾಡು ಗದಗ, ಲಕ್ಕುಂಡಿಯ ೫೦ಕ್ಕೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ದೇವಾಲಯಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ೧೦೧ ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಿಗಳು, ಕುಮಾರವ್ಯಾಸ ಭಾರತ ರಚಿಸಿದ ವೀರನಾರಾಯಣ ದೇವಾಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಖ್ಯಾತ.

destinations.name: Lakkundi Heritage Complex & Stepwells (Kalyanis)
destinations.description: An open-air museum holding 50+ Chalukyan and Hoysala temples and 101 intricately carved stepped wells (kalyanis). Highlights include the 1007 CE Brahma Jinalaya, the ornate Kasi Vishveshwara Temple with filigree door frames, and the breathtaking Musukinabavi stepped tank with subterranean shrines.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Ancient mint town (Lokkigundi) of the Western Chalukyas, Kalachuris, and Hoysalas; struck the gold coin 'Lokki-gadyana'. Mentioned in numerous 11th-century Kannada stone inscriptions.
destinations.culturalImportance: Legendary center of Jain Basadi architecture sponsored by noblewoman Attimabbe, celebrated in Kannada literature as 'Dana Chintamani'.

destinations.name: Veeranarayana Temple, Gadag (Kumara Vyasa Smaraka)
destinations.description: A historic 11th-century temple complex showing Chalukya, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara architectural phases. Here, beside a specific stone pillar in the Garuda Gamba hall, the immortal Kannada poet Kumara Vyasa sat in divine trance and composed his epic 'Karnata Bharata Kathamanjari' (Gadugina Bharata).
destinations.historicalSignificance: Originally built in 1117 CE by Hoysala King Vishnuvardhana after his conversion to Vaishnavism under Saint Ramanujacharya.
destinations.culturalImportance: The sanctum of classical Kannada poetry; revered by every student of Kannada literature.
destinations.nearestBusStation: Gadag KSRTC Old Bus Stand (1 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Central city road, easily reached by auto or foot
destinations.safetyInstructions: Remove footwear before entering temple gopuram. Peaceful and contemplative environment.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Active temple managed by Endowments Department; open to all
